subject: Acme - Observability & Inference API comparison / next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@acme.com>, Jason Wu <jason.wu@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - post-demo recap and next tests

Hi Sofia / Jason 

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we covered (TL;DR)
- Your primary goals: reduce inference unit cost, get predictable p95 latency for interactive features, and better per-route cost visibility for product analytics.
- Current comparison targets: Hyperscaler A (Vertex/Bedrock), Hyperscaler B, and an in-house microservice approach.
- Observability needs: token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, traceable request -> model call linkage, and retention for 90 days.

Redwood differentiators we highlighted
- Unified runtime across hosted / dedicated / private (so you can start hosted and later move to private without changing APIs)
- Cost levers: automatic prefix/KV caching, batching policies and quantization recommendations tied to workload
- Observability: per-request token breakdowns, per-route dashboards, trace traces that join app traces -> model calls, and rollup exports for BI.

Proposed next tests (we think these will answer your questions quickly)
1) Latency/throughput head-to-head using a short Acme workload (your sample prompt set) vs Hyperscaler A & B -> capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
2) Observability walkthrough + export: show per-route dashboards, live traces, and token-cost attribution for the same requests.
3) End-to-end SLO run: validate p95 < 200ms under expected concurrency (you mentioned ~150 RPS for the feature).

Attachments: 
- redwood-vs-hyperscalers-comparison.pdf (summary deck)
- observability-checklist.xlsx (questions and retention requirements)
- acme-testplan.md (proposed test harness + sample scripts)

Next steps / asks for you
- Can you confirm the sample prompt set + where we should pull artifacts (S3 / internal bucket)?
- Confirm the Hyperscaler endpoints you want included in the head-to-head (names + regions).
- Do you have an SSO or upload method for us to get short-term test access to your environment if needed?

We can run the tests as early as next week if that works for you  Marcus (cc'd) will own the technical run and Neha will handle logistics.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Jason Wu <jason.wu@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - post-demo recap and next tests

Thanks Marissa  helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Observability: our main ask is token-level cost attribution per product route (we need to show business owners $/engagement). Also want traces that link the user request (our API) through to the model call and back.
- Benchmarks: please include GCP Vertex and AWS Bedrock in the head-to-head. For region, use us-west-2 and us-east-1.
- SLO: our product goal is p95 ≤ 200ms for the interactive flow at 150 RPS, so please capture that.
- Data residency: anything stored for observability needs to stay in the US; can you confirm retention locations?

We can provide the prompt set and test corpus in an S3 bucket  I'll share details with Marcus.

Jason
Jason Wu
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
jason.wu@acme.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Wu <jason.wu@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - post-demo recap and next tests

Hi Jason / Marissa —

Thanks — this all sounds good. Technical plan below and what we'll need from your side.

Proposed technical test plan (high level)
1) Head-to-head harness: we will run your sample prompt set against (a) Redwood hosted API (standard config), (b) Redwood Dedicated variant (to show dedicated throughput profile), (c) GCP Vertex, (d) AWS Bedrock. We'll capture token usage, latency (p50/p95/p99), and tail behavior.
2) Observability export: we'll enable per-request tracing and token-level logs and produce an export you can import into your BI (CSV + JSONL). We'll also provision a per-route dashboard and a live walkthrough.
3) SLO validation: use a load generator to ramp to 150 RPS and capture p95 — repeat three runs and report variance.

Required from Acme
- S3 location for the prompt set + sample workload (pre-signed or access keys for the test window).
- Confirm which model family and model size you want us to run (you said "conversational, ~3B-7B equivalence").
- Approve test window: proposed Oct 21 (observability + small run) and Oct 22 (full load test) — two 2–4 hour windows.

Deliverables
- Raw metrics CSVs and a short summary report (including token-cost modeling).
- Live demo of the observability dashboard (we'll record).
- Test scripts (you can run in-house later) and a short README.

Notes on data residency and retention
- Observability exports will be stored in Redwood's US region when the tests run (we'll push CSV/JSONL directly to your S3 if you prefer). Retention on our side can be configured; by default we retain 30 days for test artifacts unless you request longer.

I'll prepare the harness and share a Drive folder with scripts and results. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cacme-observability (will grant access to the emails on this thread).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
[Attachment: acme-testplan.md (MD, 8KB)]

Subject: Acme test windows + internal asks (pricing & SSO)

Internal — quick checklist before we run: 

1) Pricing ask — Neha, can you draft an initial cost estimate for the two test windows (hosted baseline + dedicated run) and an indicative monthly price if they moved to a small dedicated pool? Put numbers into the attached pricing template.
2) SSO / access — Rishi, Marcus needs short-term S3 access to pull the corpus. Can we get an elevated download token for two days? If Acme prefers, we can push exports to their bucket instead (confirm by EOD).
3) Sales collateral — I'll send a short one-pager comparing token-cost attribution vs the hyperscalers to include with the deliverables.

Goal: have pricing + access confirmed by EOD Oct 20 so Marcus can start the runs on Oct 21.

Thanks,
Marissa
